newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares run out of steam at bourse open.
newsitem.headline: German shares run out of steam at bourse open.

text.p: German shares opened floor trade on Tuesday slightly lower, running out of steam after surging to new highs in bourse and electronic trade on Monday.

The DAX index of Germany's leading 30 blue chip shares slipped 2.42 points in early trading to 2,627.45, trading mostly flat after having cruised past the 2,600 threshold for the first time on Monday.
Volumes were described by dealers as very weak and possibly indicating some discomfort with the new record levels.
"Some market players clearly do not trust recent developments too much, there is a degree of scepticism out there," one said, forecasting a continuation of light morning losses.

But he added that the fact that the rally -- based largely on sentiment that U.S. interest rates were now not likely to move upwards as fast as some had been predicting -- had taken some players by surprise meant that some follow-through buying could lend further support to the market.
"There is a lot of under-investment out there now," he said, adding that he expected shares to tick up higher after the start of floor trading.
German DAX futures, where trading was more animated, were dealt 3.5 points lower at 2,627.5 for the September contract, due to expire by the end of this week.

U.S. August capacity utilisation and industrial production figures due at 1315 GMT, while not as critical for inflation as last week's consumer and producer price data, were seen as having a possible effect on the market later on.

Movements among individual stocks were limited. Chemical group Schering AG traded 25 pfennigs down at 113.75 marks despite receiving European Union approval for a venture with Gehe AG to acquire joint control of east German drugs group Janapharm.
